title: Recognizing 10 Years of Innovation with Equifax Academic Partnerships
summary: Equifax partners with top universities to research and develop next-generation data science solutions for customers and consumers.
body_text: People Recognizing 10 Years of Innovation with Equifax Academic Partnerships July 13, 2026 Through its Academic Partnerships program, Equifax collaborates with top universities to research and develop next-generation data science solutions. To continue pushing the boundaries of what is possible, the organization partners with leading academic institutions to give students hands-on experience using Equifax differentiated data to solve real-world business problems. Since 2016, these course-long capstone projects are undertaken by students at the end of their academic programs and give them an opportunity to apply what they’ve learned in the classroom to create a real-life customer-focused solution. “The Equifax academic partnership program allows us to continually work with university professors and their students to bring a fresh perspective to solving business challenges while simultaneously giving students a competitive edge in their future careers through hands-on access to exclusive data and advanced technology,” said Gail Wetzel, Vice President of Data & Analytics at Equifax. “The program has resulted in over 40 completed capstone projects, 11 foundational patents filed by Equifax from its work with universities, and invaluable experience for the data and analytic leaders of the future.” Recent projects from the spring 2026 semester tackled a range of current complex challenges, from data quality automation to explainable AI modeling: Georgia Tech A team of students from the Scheller College of Business Steven A. Denning Technology & Management program focused on the development of Bilinear Self-Attention Regression (BSAR). This explainable AI architecture is tailored for analyzing consumer credit data, specifically addressing the "black box" limitations of traditional AI. The students created a novel, interpretable model that offers high predictive accuracy alongside transparent decision reasoning. The transformer-based models achieved substantial improvements on datasets related to payment grids and credit utilization. Also at Georgia Tech, students in the Quantitative Computational Finance (QCF) program developed explainable, attention-based modeling for credit risk using BSAR Transformers. By analyzing raw credit data, including 24-month utilization and payment behavior sequences, the team achieved a 9.3% performance lift over traditional models. They laid the foundations for translating complex AI attributes into understandable concepts. The project delivered reusable infrastructure to explore how to make AI attributes analyst-friendly and ready for governance-compliant deployment. University of Georgia Students in the Terry College of Business’ MS in Business Analytics program focused on developing an internal dashboard to enhance operational insights into the Equifax Ignite® platform . By centralizing disparate data sources through advanced analytics and visualization, the team created a unified interface for monitoring customer engagement. The dashboard enables the proactive management of account health and the effective identification of potential churn risks. The project established a robust technical framework for future AI-driven capabilities, such as predictive scoring and anomaly detection. Emory University In the Goizueta Business School’s MS in Business Analytics program, the capstone project included creating a streamlined workflow to automate manual data quality validation processes. The team developed a three-layer pipeline that executed deterministic checks, provided diagnostic remediation, and integrated human-in-the-loop approvals. By shifting from a manual process to an intelligent, configuration-driven automation, the team reduced the time requirements of a core component of validation from weeks to hours. This implementation will lower operational costs, standardize high-quality governance documentation, and accelerate model deployment. University of Central Florida Students in the Barry S. Miller College of Business' MS in FinTech program completed two separate advanced projects. The first project estimated the effect of government intervention programs on consumer default risk using causal machine learning. The second project focused on synthetic identity fraud detection via address intelligence, equipping businesses with new ways to identify and stop sophisticated fraud attempts. These capstone projects demonstrate the power of collaboration between industry and academia. By partnering with universities, Equifax gains access to cutting-edge research and fresh perspectives, while students gain valuable real-world experience and the opportunity to make a real impact. Groundbreaking research is one step in creating industry-leading data solutions. Learn how Equifax approaches the development of new innovations . title: Centrus Energy Invited to Join S&P SmallCap 600 Index
summary: Inclusion reflects Centrus’ growing role in advancing U.S. energy security by strengthening America’s nuclear fuel supply chain.
body_text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE July 7, 2026 Centrus Energy Invited to Join S&P SmallCap 600 Index Inclusion reflects Centrus’ growing role in advancing U.S. energy security by strengthening America’s nuclear fuel supply chain. BETHESDA, Md. — Centrus Energy Corp. (NYSE: LEU), a trusted American supplier of nuclear fuel and services, today announced that the company is set to join the S&P SmallCap 600 Index, effective prior to the opening of trading on Tuesday, July 14, 2026. The company’s inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 marks an important milestone for Centrus as it works to restore America’s domestic uranium enrichment capabilities, strengthen the U.S. nuclear fuel supply chain, and support the nation’s long-term energy security and energy independence. “Centrus is proud to play a leading role in rebuilding our nation’s domestic nuclear fuel infrastructure at a time when reliable, affordable and secure sources of American energy are more important than ever,” said Amir Vexler, President and CEO of Centrus. “Our invitation into the S&P SmallCap 600 reflects the progress our team has made and the expanding role that Centrus will play in fueling the future of nuclear energy here at home and around the world.” Late last year, Centrus launched domestic centrifuge manufacturing to support a major expansion of its uranium enrichment plant in Piketon, Ohio, which is expected to create thousands of jobs across the United States. The expansion will help meet to meet the growing need for commercial Low-Enriched Uranium (LEU) for the existing fleet of nuclear reactors; commercial High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU), an advanced nuclear fuel needed by many next-generation reactor designs; as well as enriched uranium needed for national security missions. The anticipated multi-billion-dollar scope would make the expansion one of the largest nuclear infrastructure construction projects underway in the United States today. Last week, Centrus announced that it has signed a contract to finalize the terms of the competitively-awarded, $900 million task order it received earlier this year from the U.S. Department of Energy. The S&P SmallCap 600 is designed to measure the small-cap segment of the U.S. equity market. Inclusion in the index follows S&P Dow Jones Indices’ announcement that Centrus will replace Whitestone REIT in the index. About Centrus Energy Centrus Energy is a trusted American supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry, helping meet the growing need for clean, affordable, carbon-free energy. Since 1998, the Company has provided its utility customers with more than 1,850 reactor years of fuel, which is equivalent to more than 7 billion tons of coal. With world-class technical and engineering capabilities, Centrus is pioneering production of High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium and is leading the effort to restore America’s uranium enrichment capabilities at scale so that we can meet our clean energy, energy security, and national security needs. Find out more at www.centrusenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn and X . title: What Is Invoice Reconciliation & How to Automate It at Scale
summary: Invoice reconciliation matches invoice details against POs and receiving records to confirm accuracy before payment. Learn how to automate it for faster, error-free processing.
body_text: Invoice reconciliation is the process of matching invoice details, such as amounts, vendor information, and line items, against purchase orders and receiving records to confirm everything is accurate before any payment is made. Traditionally, this means manually cross-checking each invoice, tracking down missing documents, and resolving mismatches. However, this approach can quickly become a bottleneck at scale, preventing FinOps teams from working efficiently. This is why automating invoice reconciliation has become essential for growing businesses, and Fintelite might be just the tool you’re looking for. What Is Invoice Reconciliation? As a core function within accounts payable, invoice reconciliation sits between the receipt of a supplier’s invoice and the release of payment. Its purpose is to confirm that what is being billed accurately reflects what was ordered and received. Every time an invoice is received, reconciliation is used to: Match the invoice against the purchase order and receiving records Verify that quantities, amounts, and pricing align with the agreed terms Cross-check vendor details to confirm the invoice is legitimate Flag any discrepancies, such as overcharges, duplicates, or mismatches Approve clean, validated invoice for payment Record the transaction accurately in the ledger By conducting these steps, businesses can prevent losses due to overpayments, whether caused by pricing errors or unauthorized charges. How Invoice Reconciliation Applies Across Business Sectors While the underlying goal stays the same, the way invoice reconciliation is applied can vary by industry. Differences in transaction volume, complexity, and compliance requirements often influence how teams handle the process in practice. Retail Retail businesses often manage frequent inventory restocks across multiple locations, which means a high volume of invoices moving through the system regularly. Reconciliation typically involves matching supplier invoices against purchase orders, verifying that unit costs and quantities align with what was actually received in-store or at the warehouse. Manufacturing Manufacturers source raw materials and components from a wide network of suppliers. Reconciliation in this setting helps confirm that invoiced quantities match delivery records and that pricing remains consistent with long-term supplier contracts. Healthcare In healthcare, reconciliation checks that invoices for medical supplies, equipment, and services align with procurement approvals. With multiple departments ordering supplies independently, this process helps keep spending accurate and properly accounted for. Supply Chain & Logistics Invoices in supply chain and logistics are often tied to variable costs, such as freight, warehousing, and fulfillment services. Reconciliation verifies that billed charges correspond to agreed rates and the service levels actually delivered. Want to speed up extracting and reviewing invoices across POs and receipts? See how you can bulk automate invoice reconciliation with Fintelite. Book a demo Common Challenges in Invoice Reconciliation Manual reconciliation puts a lot of pressure on accuracy, especially as invoice volume grows. Here are several challenges that often occur when handling invoice reconciliation routinely. Data Entry Errors Manual data entry is highly susceptible to typos, misread amounts, which can lead to incorrect payments. High Workload With the growing volume of invoices, reconciliation demands more time and manpower, pulling finance teams away from higher-value work. Inconsistent Accuracy Manual checks are prone to error, as review quality shifts from person to person and tends to decline over long hours due to fatigue. Delayed Approvals Invoices are often routed through physical paperwork, email, or disconnected spreadsheets. This leaves approvals dependent on manual follow-up, often leading to days-long waits. How to Automate Invoice Reconciliation The repetitive process of manually matching invoices quietly drains your time and resources. It’s time to automate invoice reconciliation, and it’s easier than it sounds. With Fintelite, teams can build a workflow that extracts, matches, and validates invoices automatically based on your specific rules, with human-in-the-loop review where it matters. Here’s how to set it up. 1. Choose the Required Document Set the workflow to begin by uploading all required documents, such as an invoice, receipt, purchase order, or other records you want to include as part of the reconciliation process. 2. Define Extraction Fields Fintelite’s AI OCR extracts every key field from any document type by default. But, you can also customize specific fields to extract, such as vendor name, invoice number, amount, quantities, and payment terms. 3. Tailor Your Validation Rules Set rules to check extracted invoice data against purchase orders and receiving records, such as acceptable price variance, quantity thresholds, or required field checks. From cross-document validation to field-existence checks, all easily configurable without code. 4. Establish Approval Routing Decide when human-in-the-loop review is necessary, such as for mismatches or amounts exceeding a set limit, and route those exceptions to the right approver. For validated results, choose whether they still need a final approval gate or can move straight to export. 5. Publish & Run the Workflow Once configured, publish the workflow to start running it advanced automatically. From that point on, invoices are processed end-to-end, pausing only when human review is triggered. Benefits of Automating Invoice Reconciliation Moving reconciliation away from manual checks brings advantages. Here’s what you can expect from automating. Significant Time Savings Extraction, matching, and validation happen automatically in minutes, saving hours of manual efforts. Same-Day Approvals With flagged exceptions routed straight to the right reviewer, approvals no longer sit waiting in email threads. Most invoices can move from received to approved within the same day. Reduced Risk of Duplicate or Overpayments Consistent validation rules automatically catch duplicate invoices and mismatched amounts. This prevents money from going out the door for something that was never owed. Scales Seamlessly Without Hiring As transaction volume grows, the workflow keeps pace without requiring additional headcount. Reconciliation stays consistent whether you’re processing dozens or thousands of invoices a month. [FAQs] More About Invoice Reconciliation What is invoice reconciliation? Invoice reconciliation is the process of matching invoice details against purchase orders and receiving records to confirm accuracy before payment. Can invoice reconciliation be fully automated? Most of the process can be automated, though human-in-the-loop review is important for exception handling when invoices contain discrepancies, missing documents, or values that fall outside expected thresholds. How does automation handle mismatched invoices? Mismatched invoices are automatically flagged and routed to the right team member for manual review before payment is released. Is automated invoice reconciliation only for large companies? No, automation can scale to fit both small teams and high-volume finance operations, making it just as useful for growing businesses as it is for larger ones.

title: Tablevibe and Xendit partner to offer Filipino restaurants free online ordering system
body_text: Press release - 1 December 2022: Y-Combinator-backed startup Tablevibe has partnered with Xendit to launch its commission-free online ordering system in The Philippines. The restaurant tech venture successfully launched in Metro Manila following a surge in demand for its solutions in Singapore and Australia. The move empowers any restaurant to set up a free webshop and accept pickup and delivery orders directly from its customers. On-demand drivers are sourced automatically and deliver food in a 10-kilometer radius for a PHP60 flat fee. As a result, restaurants can save up to 70% in online food ordering costs. Helping eateries engage directly with digital diners One of Tablevibe’s launch partners is CloudEats , a rapidly expanding cloud kitchen group with operations in both the Philippines and Vietnam. Kimberly Yao , CEO of CloudEats adds: "Tablevibe helps us engage directly with our loyal customers, creates seamless commerce experiences, and offers great delivery fulfillment rates. It’s an exciting new channel for us.” Restaurants typically use their cost savings to partially cover delivery fees, resulting in lower prices for consumers. Tablevibe’s deep integration with last-mile delivery services allows restaurants to deliver orders instantly without hiring their own drivers. Enabling restaurants to ride a new wave of digitization Xendit , a leading payment gateway in The Philippines, partnered with Tablevibe to spearhead its expansion. Xendit’s Managing Director Yang Yang Zhang mentions: “Our partnership with Tablevibe marks an essential step on our mission to build the digital infrastructure for Philippine-based businesses. It enables restaurants to accept payments via credit cards, debit cards, and e-Wallets like GCash through a single integration. Together, we’re excited to support eateries and boost their online sales across the country.” ‍ Direct-to-consumer is the future of the F&B industry The global pandemic drove a seismic shift toward digital commerce in the Food & Beverage (F&B) industry. 70% of consumers say they prefer ordering directly with restaurants, but most F&B operators need more tools to unlock direct-to-consumer relationships. Mathieu Sneep, Tablevibe's Chief Operation Officer (COO) says, “We saw our global revenue surge more than 500% year over year. Together with our strong local partners, we are incredibly excited about supporting local restaurants and making their offerings even more accessible to food lovers across The Philippines.” About Tablevibe Tablevibe's mission is to help restaurants go direct-to-consumer. The Singaporean startup was part of Y Combinator's summer 2021 batch and received $1.5M in funding from venture capital investors like Global Founders Capital and Velocity Ventures . ‍Since its official launch in early 2021, the startup partnered with hundreds of restaurants from industry leaders like Les Amis Group , The Bistro Group , CloudEats , Vascobelo , and Burger & Lobster . Tablevibe's founding team consists of ex-Google business leaders ( Jeroen Rutten and Mathieu Sneep ) and a former lead teacher from coding school Le Wagon ( Guido Caldara ). For more information or press related inquires, please contact hello@tablevibe.co

title: The Toro Company reinforces long term investment in the European golf industry through expanded partnership with GCAE
body_text: Change Language If you are a customer with a product-related inquiry, please contact us at www.toro.com/customer-support/contact . If you are a member of the media, please contact the appropriate individual shown below: The Toro Company reinforces long term investment in the European golf industry through expanded partnership with GCAE Apr 27, 2026 | Golf The Toro Company, a global leader in turf, irrigation and landscape solutions, is expanding its partnership with the Golf Course Association Europe (GCAE). Building on years of collaboration, the renewed agreement places more emphasis on knowledge-sharing and practical support for golf facilities across Europe. Toro is known for its broad portfolio of equipment, irrigation and smart technologies, but equally as much for its investment in people: greenkeeper education programmes, industry scholarships, training initiatives and long-term collaboration with professional associations. The expanded partnership adds a new layer to that commitment by connecting Toro’s expertise even more closely to the owners and operators who shape the future of the industry. At the GCAE Golf Business Conference in Madeira last year, Toro contributed to the programme with a presentation on water management and the operational impact of changing resource conditions. The response from delegates underlined how relevant Toro’s experience is for facilities that want to combine playing quality with responsible use of water and other inputs. Through the strengthened partnership, Toro gains a more structured platform in Europe to share practical experience, support informed decision making and engage in deeper dialogue with facilities and industry leaders. This collaboration reflects a shared focus on helping golf operations remain resilient, responsible and commercially strong. “Supporting the golf industry has always been central to how Toro operates,” said Andrew Ihrke, Senior International Marketing Manager at The Toro Company. “By deepening our partnership with GCAE, we are reinforcing our long-term investment in European golf and strengthening our ability to share real-world experience around innovation, education and sustainable course management. It is about working alongside facilities to support the long-term success of the industry” “The conversations that happen at GCAE events are different from most. You are in a room with the people who actually run the business of golf — owners, operators, decision-makers. That is exactly where we want to be. It keeps us sharp, and it helps us make sure that what we build and offer actually fits what the industry needs.” said Andy Brown, Senior Sales Manager Global Business Development and Relationships at The Toro Company. Renate Roeleveld, CEO of GCAE: “Toro has always been more than machines. They invest in people, in knowledge and in the long-term health of the game. This partnership helps connect their day-to-day experience on the course with the decisions that shape how facilities are run. Together we can share insights, ask better questions and help facilities move towards strong, sustainable and future-ready operations.” Together, Toro and GCAE aim to support the European golf sector with practical guidance and shared expertise so facilities can deliver great golf today and build a resilient industry for tomorrow. Notes to editors About Golf Course Association Europe (GCAE) Golf Course Association Europe represents golf course owners and operators across Europe. GCAE supports facilities through data, knowledge and advocacy and provides a platform for sharing expertise and best practices among professionals who run the business of golf. title: How HR Teams Can Help Avoid AI Scams
summary: AI scams are tricking HR teams with messages and fake candidates. Spot signs, fix gaps, and protect your hiring process.
body_text: AI scams are becoming harder for HR teams to spot, and the financial impact is growing. The scale of the problem is already significant: Forbes recently reported that the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s IC3 unit received more than 22,000 AI fraud complaints in 2025, with adjusted losses topping $893 million. Scammers are using AI to send fraudulent messages, create fake candidates, and impersonate executives or employees. These attacks are becoming more realistic, more personalized, and more difficult to identify. As the technology continues to evolve, HR teams need strong verification processes and the ability to recognize clear warning signs to help stop them before they cause damage. Spot Fake Applicants and Suspicious Communications Traditional advice like “watch for typos” no longer works. As scams become more convincing, HR teams can no longer rely on instinct alone. Strong processes and careful verification are just as important as recognizing warning signs. Watch for Highly polished phishing emails that contain unusual requests, reference internal information the sender should not know, request sensitive data, or attempt to bypass normal procedures. Messages, calls, or videos that appear to come from leadership and demand urgent action, confidential information, or exceptions to established processes. Applicant profiles or resumes with inconsistent work histories, credentials that are difficult to verify, or vague descriptions of past experience. Communications t hat look and sound like they came from your organization but originate from unfamiliar sources. Trust the Process, Not the Message Even the most convincing AI scam is far less effective when organizations follow clear verification procedures. Strong processes help reduce the risk that a single message, rushed decision, or moment of inattention leads to a costly mistake. When evaluating candidates, verify identities through secure systems, confirm employment history through trusted sources, and ask follow-up questions about projects, timelines, and past responsibilities. These steps can help uncover inconsistencies that might otherwise go unnoticed. If a request involves sensitive information, payroll changes , or exceptions to standard procedures, confirm it through a separate communication channel before taking action. Report suspected impersonation attempts to your IT or security team so they can investigate and help prevent future incidents. When something feels off, pause. Trust your process, not your first impression. Al Threats Evolve Rapidly: Keep Training to Stay Ahead AI scams change quickly, making it difficult for HR teams to rely on outdated training or annual cybersecurity refreshers alone. Regular training helps employees recognize emerging threats, respond appropriately, and feel more confident when something does not look right. Implement These Training Strategies: Offer short training sessions throughout the year on emerging AI scam trends Run realistic phishing simulations that reflect HR-specific scenarios Use real-world examples to help employees practice identifying suspicious activity Reinforce when and how employees should report potential scams Create a culture where employees feel comfortable pausing, asking questions, and verifying information before acting Get Ahead of AI Scams With CBIZ AI scams are not slowing down. Connect with a CBIZ advisor who can help you develop the right approach to help protect your organization. Frequently Asked Questions Always verify using a secondary, trusted channel: Call the employee using known contact info, require changes through a secure HRIS portal and enforce multi-step approval for payroll updates. Scammers often target the information that can help them steal money, impersonate employees, or gain access to systems. That can include, changing employee direct deposit information, finding ways to gain access to Social Security numbers, bank account details, , benefits elections, tax documents, employee identification numbers, personal contact information, and login credentials. HR should treat requests involving this information as high risk, and should take additional steps to verify the request . An effective response plan should not sit with HR alone. HR should work with information technology, cybersecurity, legal, compliance, payroll, benefits, communications, and leadership to define who reviews suspicious requests, who approves next steps, and who contacts affected employees if needed. Clear ownership helps the organization move quickly without creating confusion, overreacting, or missing important reporting obligations. © Copyright CBIZ, Inc. All rights reserved. body_text: View All News Everus to Acquire Epsilon Industries, Premier Off-Site Modular Construction Solutions Provider July 31, 2026 Strengthens Off-Site Modular Construction Offerings Enhances Geographic and Market Exposure Attractive Growth Profile BISMARCK, N.D.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Everus Construction Group (NYSE: ECG) announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Epsilon Industries, a premier designer and manufacturer of complex, modular mechanical and electrical building infrastructure systems, for $295 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments. With more than 25 years of experience providing off-site construction solutions across North America, Epsilon is recognized in the industry for its innovation, proprietary capabilities and highly refined execution processes that provide consistent and efficient delivery of complex custom solutions. Epsilon offers a full range of services, including design-assist, custom fabrication and turnkey field installation that support diverse project types across attractive end markets, including data center, advanced manufacturing and healthcare. Epsilon has an extensive footprint of off-site modular construction capabilities across multiple strategic facilities in the U.S. and Canada, enabling nationwide distribution. In addition to integrating with Everus’ existing geographic footprint, Everus expects that Epsilon’s capabilities will enhance growth in priority geographic areas, including Florida, Texas, the Mid-Atlantic and the Northeast. Epsilon is led by a strong leadership team with extensive technical and operational expertise and has an experienced labor force that includes more than 50 engineers and 120 skilled trade employees. “Epsilon has a strong legacy of innovation and execution in off-site construction services, and the addition of their team will expand our capabilities as we continue to deepen our focus on modular construction and prefabrication across our operations to meet customers’ growing demand,” said Jeffrey S. Thiede, president and CEO of Everus. “Off-site construction in controlled shop environments supports safer work conditions, helps us use labor and materials more efficiently, and creates more predictable project outcomes. Epsilon will help expand our geographic reach and further strengthen our position in key end markets. Together, we are in a stronger position to take advantage of the attractive market dynamics in our business.” Epsilon President Chris Wiederick said, “We’re thrilled to join the Everus team, and we look forward to collaborating with Everus’ off-site construction leaders to share best practices and support existing operations with off-site solutions for the complex, diverse projects that Everus builds. This is an exciting time in our industry, and we are confident that as part of Everus, we will be able to further accelerate our next phase of growth.” Wiederick and other key members of Epsilon’s experienced leadership team are expected to remain with the company. Financial and Transaction Overview Everus will acquire Epsilon for $295 million, subject to certain customary closing adjustments. The acquisition will be funded through a combination of cash on hand and borrowings under the company's credit facilities. The transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. Epsilon has a proven history of strong growth with an attractive margin and free cash flow profile. For the full calendar year 2026, Epsilon expects to generate revenue of approximately $250 million with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) as a percentage of revenue in the low double digits. Everus will update its 2026 financial forecast following the successful close of the transaction. Compelling Transaction Rationale Meaningfully enhances Everus' off-site construction offerings. Epsilon’s turnkey off-site construction capabilities support complex mechanical and electrical projects through in-house engineering, design and manufacturing, underpinned by a proven, committed and tenured management team with more than 25 years of operating experience. Adds an extensive footprint of modular prefabrication capacity, expanding access to attractive geographic markets. With nationwide distribution, Epsilon enhances access to priority geographic markets for Everus, including Florida, Texas, the Mid-Atlantic and the Northeast. Advances Everus’ strategic objective of expanding and diversifying end-market exposure. title: Lab Chemical Relocation: Hidden Risks and How to Avoid Them
summary: Read about the hidden risks involved in chemical material and lab relocation projects, and how to avoid them by partnering with experts!
body_text: Lab chemical relocation is common when facilities expand or research operations consolidate and can even be a routine step in a multi-site pharmaceutical workflow. The process may seem straightforward at first glance, but it’s more challenging than simply moving bottles from origin to destination. Every lab chemical relocation carries serious operational, safety, and regulatory risks like chemical spills, regulatory violations, compromised material integrity, and personal injury. These risks can significantly impact research continuity and quality compliance. Because of this, lab chemical relocation isn’t simply a logistics matter. Nor is it a suitable task for general moving companies who lack the knowledge and capabilities to proactively mitigate these risks. Instead, trust your chemicals and lab assets to lab relocation specialists. Moving lab chemicals is a complex and multi-layered process that can be governed by federal and state laws, institutional policies, and even basic chemistry principles. On top of this, cold chain material relocation includes the extra criteria for consistent temperature control. Errors and deviations from guidelines and plans can range from timely to costly to a worst-case catastrophic consequence. Understanding the hidden risks involved in chemical material and lab relocation projects is the first step toward protecting valuable laboratory assets and ensuring a straightforward move. Risk #1 Regulatory Compliance Safety data sheets (SDS) and material safety data sheets (MSDS) are well known to anyone working in the lab, but once that chemical leaves the facility bound for a new destination, different regulations are added to the equation. Depending on the material, lab relocation specialists may need to be trained on and compliant with regulations from U.S. governmental agencies like the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), the Department of Transportation (DOT), and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)1. Penalties for non-compliance can range from fines to civil action in federal court, and even imprisonment2. State and international regulations may introduce further complexity that must be navigated. These combined regulations underscore the need to work with trained lab chemical relocation experts that understand how to safely and efficiently move your chemical materials while adhering to multiple guidelines. Risk #2 Chain-of-Custody When moving laboratory chemicals, maintaining traceability and accountability is essential. This includes clearly documenting incoming and outgoing handoffs, the truck’s route, actions taken by individual lab relocation specialists, and precise location of each container. During a cold chain material relocation, tracking consistent and precise temperature is vital. Any excursions during the move can alter chemical properties, degrade compounds, and compromise experimental reliability. Lab relocation specialists manage temperature sensitive material moves using vehicles with multiple power and freezer redundancies, on-board generators, and other precautions to strengthen the chain-of-custody. This provides confidence that chemicals and sensitive materials are fully protected throughout the lab chemical relocation process. Risk #3 Packaging and Chemical Compatibility Improper packaging can easily lead to a chemical transport incident. Chemical containers may appear sealed, undamaged, and properly labeled, yet when subject to normal vehicle vibrations and pressure changes, these cumulative stressors might elevate the risk of leaks, spills, and contamination. At the same time, if incompatible chemicals, like acids and bases or flammables and oxidizers, are packed together or insufficiently contained during a lab chemical relocation, a serious breach could result in catastrophic and life-threatening consequences for the movers and the surrounding communities. A chemical and laboratory relocation company with deep experience and chemical knowledge will use packaging specifically designed for hazardous and laboratory chemicals, and segregate incompatible and reactive materials. They will also ensure that containers are properly stabilized to minimize movement during the trip. Risk #4 Unknown or Legacy Chemicals As lab operations evolve or researchers change roles, some reagents, samples, and other chemicals may be pushed to the side, never to be used again. The same can happen when a label is compromised. These unknown “legacy chemicals” present a risk because the material cannot be properly classified, packaged, or documented. Simply moving an unknown material along with everything else is not advisable, and in fact, attempting to transport an unknown chemical may violate federal law and increase safety risks. Need help identifying and organizing[TK1.1] your full cold storage inventory? Start with a Better Storage Management assessment. Use our Cold Storage Unit Savings Calculator for an instant estimate Risk #5 Time Delays Time is a constant pressure, and unfortunately, this pressure may be an incentive to cut corners. When it comes to lab chemical relocation or a full laboratory relocation, the consequences of rushing steps like vetting qualified laboratory relocation specialists, documenting inventory, and more in the interest of time can result in productivity, safety, financial, and legal ramifications that ripple throughout the company. Early planning is the best way to reduce time pressures. Take the time to align all internal stakeholders on a coordinated logistics plan. Share the plan details with external vendors like a lab relocation specialist so that they have ample opportunity to provide early-stage guidance and begin preparations. Benefits Beyond Protecting Chemicals Lab chemicals are a foundation of critical research, testing, development, and manufacturing activities. Efficiently relocating them while sustaining safety and compliance requires skills and expertise beyond what a general mover can offer. By identifying and mitigating hidden risks early in a relocation project, laboratories are in a better position to protect sensitive materials, maintain compliance, and avoid costly disruptions. When partnering with lab relocation specialists, organizations can further mitigate risks to ensure their chemical or lab relocation proceeds smoothly from start to finish.
